title: Mechanism underlying the antioxidant activity of taurine

sections.abstract: <jats:p> Taurine is an ubiquitous sulfur‐containing amino acid found in high concentration in the heart. Although it has antioxidant activity, it is not a classical free radical scavenger, therefore, its mechanism remains unclear. Recently we proposed that taurine prevents the formation of superoxide by the mitochondria, a mechanism related to the formation of a post‐transcriptional modification of tRNA <jats:sup>Leu(UUR)</jats:sup> in the mitochondria. By decreasing its post‐transcriptional wobble modification, taurine deficiency reduces the levels of respiratory chain subunits, thereby diminishing respiratory chain complex activity and oxygen consumption. As predicted, taurine‐depleted hearts are oxidativestressed, as exemplified by decreased aconitase activity and the glutathione redox ratio. Among other damage, taurine deficiency triggers cell death, as shown by an increase in the percentage of apoptotic cells. Because the antioxidant, Tiron, prevents apoptosis in taurine deficient cardiomyocytes in culture, cell death is attributable to oxidative stress. In conclusion, this study confirms the potential role of taurine as an antioxidant, but not as a radical scavenger. Rather, taurine ensures an efficient flux of reducing equivalents through the respiratory chain, thereby preventing the diversion of electrons to the acceptor oxygen, resulting in the formation of reactive oxygen species. This work was supported by AHA grant. </jats:p>
